## Gates

Test execution policy comes from `.tt.toml` at the checkout's top level, read by the
vendored `tools/tt`. It sets `automatic_broad = false`: the broad targets below are
skipped locally unless forced, and hosted CI is the routine broad verification.
`just test-one <pytest args>` is the focused route (paths relative to `python/`).
`just check-hygiene` (ops-check, ops-docs check, `tasks check`) always runs. The broad targets, which a policy may
skip and record as skipped, never passed, are `check-code` (ruff, pyright), `test` (the
full suite, including the suites the fast loop excludes; it forwards pytest arguments, as
in `just test -rs`), `test-fast` (testmon, excluding the kill-matrix, persistence-cut and
exerciser suites) and `ci-python`. `just check` runs hygiene then `check-code`, and
`just gate` runs `check` then `test`. Force broad work deliberately with
`just test-full [pytest args]` or `TT_FORCE=1 just check`. The pre-commit hook runs
hygiene then `check-code`. The pre-push hook takes `hook-pre-push-fast` (hygiene,
`check-code`, `test-fast`) when the push goes to `origin` and every pushed ref matches
`ci_suite_refs` (`refs/heads/*`, `refs/tags/v*`), and `hook-pre-push` (hygiene,
`check-code`, `test`) otherwise, warning when policy skips that suite. Either way only
hygiene runs unforced. Hook timers cover hygiene only (earlier `hook-*` timings also
covered the code checks and suite, so the series are not comparable). Hosted CI
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `just ci-python`, forced, on every pushed branch and,
through `release.yml`, on release tags, and checks its JUnit against pytest's
collection. The suite runs on xdist workers sized by `host-budget` (ops), so no test may
depend on another test's process or order.

Known coverage gaps:

- Capability-dependent tests are proven only on the certified ext4 tuple, by a suite
  run on that host (the pre-push gate while local policy is enabled; `just test-full`
  there once it is off), as `docs/durability.md` and `docs/development.md` describe.
  Hosted runs exercise that code on the runner's uncertified kernel and volume and skip
  only what the runner cannot supply; no hosted pass is certified-tuple evidence. On an
  unpaired hosted runner, 11 tests skip across 6324 collected tests: the 7
  casefold-volume tests in `test_fs_resolve_casefold.py` (`ATOMS_CASEFOLD_VOLUME` unset,
  which the certified host also skips), 3 bind-mount tests in `test_fs_binding.py` and
  `test_fs_resolve_conformance.py` (no user or mount namespaces on the runner), and 1
  allowlist record check in `test_certification_record.py` when private `records` are
  unavailable. All are capability or private-record omissions; none is a portability
  gap. Changing or diagnosing capability behaviour runs the relevant focused tests, or a
  forced suite, on the certified host.
- Recertification: a `chore/recertify-<kernel>` branch is merged only after
  `just test-full` passes on the newly certified host (`docs/development.md`).
- `just certify` never runs on hosted runners.

On a fresh clone, `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.

## Layout

- `python/src/atoms/` — `core`, `fs`, `store`, `chain`, `coordinator`; `python/tests/` —
  the suites; `python/tools/certify/` — the crash-certification harness.
- `docs/` — public reference documentation: `records.md` (data model), `protocol.md`
  (protocol), `durability.md` (standard), and `development.md` (guide).
- Task records, design specs, implementation plans, briefs, handoffs, and crash
  certification JSON evidence live in the project's `records` directory, committed in
  the `records` repository, never in this tree.

## Rules

- Authority order: `docs/records.md`, `docs/protocol.md`, and `docs/durability.md`, then
  active task design specs and plans in the project's `records` directory; where they
  disagree, the authority documents win unless the active spec explicitly revises them.
- Each file under `docs/` describes current code behaviour and conforms to
  `document-types` v1 (`[documents] standard = 1` in `identity.toml`). Update the
  relevant public document in the same commit that alters the behaviour it specifies.
